#: Fields regress.py skips: values that change from run to run (or from machine to machine), so a baseline can't pin them. Each entry has interface, method and field regexes, as differences.json's, and its reason. Found by comparing three full stand-in runs on one PC; a field that differs on CI's runner gets its entry here too.

reason: a background app's session runs OpenLamina's empty frames until the app runs one: how many have run when it asks
a background app's session runs OpenLamina's empty frames until the app runs one: whether input focus has come yet when it asks (true once on CI's Linux x86 runner, where it was false)
IsInputAvailable's opposite, and as early as it (false once on CI's Linux x64 runner, where it was true)
a background app's session runs OpenLamina's empty frames until the app runs one: whether one starts within the timeout
how many session state changes (each a SceneApplicationStateChanged) arrive before the first frame's poll: 4 to 6 on CI
its first field is the scene process id
read while a fade is running: how far it has got depends on when the call lands
a model loads on a thread of its own: a call answers Loading until the load of its name has finished, which a later call in the same run may or may not find done
the struct, compared as raw bytes, holds the mesh's vertex pointer (where the runtime has a visibility mask) and padding bytes no caller can read
whether VREvent_ProcessConnected from another test process is pending yet is timing
the runtime's adapter's LUID (for D3D) or Vulkan physical device handle, which Windows and the Vulkan loader assign afresh
the runtime's adapter's index among the machine's adapters, or -1 when it can't be told at that moment (no OpenXR instance yet, or Direct3D 9Ex not created): -1 once on CI's runner where it was 0
the time left in the current frame, measured when it's asked
the thumb's curl is eased over time towards the touch estimated from the grip and trigger: how far it has come when it's asked
